shortDescription: Bank of America NYSE:BAC, Blackstone NYSE:BX, Citi NYSE:C, and Morgan Stanley NYSE:MS are leading a $64B transaction  to finance and deploy AI compute capacity, using Broadcom's NASDAQ:AVGO technology for Anthropic (ANT), the companies said Monday.The transaction is part of a strategic compute capa…

children: to finance and deploy AI compute capacity, using Broadcom's
The transaction is part of a strategic compute capacity agreement previously announced by Broadcom
, with expected deliveries starting in calendar year 2027.

The deal will be executed through a newly formed special purpose vehicle, or SPV, with committed financing from the lead financial partners (BAC, BX, C, and MS), with Blackstone as the sole provider of the committed portion of the second lien financing. Broadcom is providing residual value support to the SPV for the amount equivalent to the first lien portion of the financing.
While investors are starting to question the sustainability of the AI boom, Blackstone's commitment reflects its confidence in demand for the technology.
"The rapidly growing demand for AI is creating an enormous opportunity to finance compute capacity at scale," said Blackstone
President and Chief Operating Officer Jon Gray. "We're proud to help advance this buildout with Broadcom."

head of banking and executive vice chair, Vis Raghavan, added, "Citi is proud to pioneer innovative structures and leverage our global capital markets structuring and distribution expertise to help accelerate the buildout of critical AI infrastructure that will power the future of technology for years to come."

title: BofA, Blackstone, Citi, Morgan Stanley lead $63B AI compute financing in pact with Broadcom
